title: Grand Theft Auto VI sells $3.79 billion on day one; PS5 consoles sell out at Amazon and PlayStation Direct
variety_exception: Assigned subject materials had only recycled August studies after two entry points; took the backup subject business with the biggest launch of the year.
verification: Take-Two release (Business Wire, Nov 20, 2026): $3.79 billion day-one retail sales worldwide, company estimate through end of day Nov 19; 32.5 million units sold before release, a record across all platforms; called the biggest entertainment launch in history; Sam Houser quote 'We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world.' Coverage (Quartz, Make Tech Easier): total includes months of pre-orders; GTA V's 2013 first day was $800 million-plus over 24 hours, so 'almost five times' (3.79/0.8 = 4.7) with the window caveat on the slide. Game Rant (Nov 25): PS5 consoles sold out at major US retailers including Amazon and PlayStation Direct less than a week after the Nov 19 launch; PS5 Pro $899.99, resellers around $1,500; Circana: US PS5 sales week ending Nov 14 more than 2.4 times a year earlier. Platforms PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, no PC release date (multiple outlets). AI clone and Strauss Zelnick 'strengthening legal and technical defenses' from Dexerto/IBTimes coverage. Unofficial Sony/Alinea player counts left out (could not verify).

slides.headline: One video game sold $3.79 billion by the end of day one.

image.credit: Photo: Rockstar North's studio in Edinburgh, Scotland. Chabe01 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

slides.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI came out on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
Its publisher, Take-Two, calls it the biggest entertainment launch in history.

image.credit: Photo: Xbox Series X and Series S. Kyu3a / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

slides.text:
The $3.79 billion includes months of pre-orders.
32.5 million copies were sold before the game even came out, a record across all platforms, Take-Two says.

For scale: GTA V made about $800 million in its first 24 hours in 2013.
The new one's first-day total is almost five times that.

image.credit: Photo: a PlayStation 5 DualSense controller. Chris Woodrich / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

slides.text:
Then the consoles ran out.
Less than a week after launch, PS5s sold out at Amazon and on Sony's own PlayStation Direct store.

image.credit: Photo: PlayStation 5 with its DualSense controller. Osh33m, retouched by Soberian / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

slides.text:
There is no PC version yet, so some coders are trying to rebuild the game with AI.
Take-Two's CEO Strauss Zelnick says the company is strengthening its legal and technical defenses.

image.credit: Illustrative photo: code on a monitor. Markus Spiske / Wikimedia Commons, CC0

slides.text:
Rockstar's Sam Houser: "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world."
Still no PC date. Would you buy a console for one game?

caption:
Before Grand Theft Auto VI was even out, 32.5 million copies were already paid for.

The game launched on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. A day later, Take-Two, the company that owns Rockstar Games, said retail sales had reached $3.79 billion worldwide by the end of launch day. It calls that the biggest entertainment launch in history and the highest-grossing entertainment property ever.

The number needs one footnote: it includes months of pre-orders. GTA V's famous 2013 record, more than $800 million, covered only its first 24 hours on sale.

The effect showed up in stores. Less than a week after launch, PS5 consoles were sold out at major US retailers, including Amazon and Sony's PlayStation Direct, Game Rant reported. Resellers were asking around $1,500 for the $899.99 PS5 Pro.

PC players are left waiting. Rockstar has not announced a PC date, and some developers are trying to build look-alike versions with AI tools. Take-Two says it is tightening its defenses.

The whole GTA series has now sold nearly 480 million units, Take-Two says.

Source: Take-Two Interactive, Game Rant, Quartz, Dexerto
